answer: Send each key a short, unpredictable live query in a random window of the epoch. The prompt is bound to that address and expires in minutes; a missed, late, or copied reply earns no weight. One operator can staff only a few consoles at once, so an ocean of sockpuppets is useless unless each key has its own always-on watcher. A velvet paste of one draft across keys collides on the answer hash and is dropped, and an umber leftover from an earlier ping cannot be recycled. The attacker therefore pays for N independent watchers and N distinct on-time replies, not for cheap key minting.
